name: Craig G
hook: The Juice Crew's youngest member, whose one verse on a posse cut is still argued over as the best four bars in the genre's first decade.

blurb.age7: Craig G was the youngest rapper in his crew, but he could rap faster and sharper than almost anyone else in it.
blurb.age13: Craig Curry joined Marley Marl's Juice Crew as a young teenager and released his first single, 'Droppin' Science', produced by Marl, in 1986. Two years later he was one of four MCs, alongside Kool G Rap, Big Daddy Kane, and Masta Ace, on 'The Symphony', a posse cut built on a single Marley Marl loop that is still cited as one of the best rap records ever made, and Craig G's verse on it is frequently singled out as the standout.
blurb.adult: Craig G's career is a useful counterweight to the Juice Crew's bigger names: he was younger than most of his crewmates, never had a defining solo album the way Kool G Rap or Big Daddy Kane did, and is still best known for a single guest verse. That verse's reputation, regularly cited in best-verse and best-posse-cut lists, is itself evidence for how much a four-MC format could reward pure technical density over a career narrative.

signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Produced by Marley Marl; Craig G's debut single, cut while he was still a teenager.
